blocks.text: The Name As-Sayyid The Lord and Master is found in a hadeeth from the Messenger of Allaah ﷺ which is recorded by Aboo Daawood with a good chain. 'Abdullaah bin ash-Shikheer said,

"I went with a deputation of Banoo 'Aamir to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we said: You are our lord (sayyid). To this he replied: The lord is Allah, the Blessed and Exalted. Then we said: And the one of us most endowed with excellence and superiority. To this he replied: Say what you have to say, or part of what you have to say, and do not let the devil make you his agents."
It comes from Ibn 'Abbaas that he said regarding the saying of Allaah,
"Allaah is As-Samad The Self-Sufficient Master (Whom all creatures need, He neither eats nor drinks).
"Indeed He is the Master who is perfect in His Mastership."

The intention of the Prophet ﷺ when he said 'Allaah is the Lord and Master' is that Mastership is in truth only for Allaah. He alone is the One to actualize mastership, ownership, creation, disposing of affairs with the creation displaying humbleness and humility. He is the Lord and Master who disposes and directs the affairs in this universe without an equal. He is the Lord and Master without partner to whom obedience, humility and humbleness is directed. So as He is the Lord and Master without equal who directs creation without a helper, it is He also who is the Lord and Master, the One who deserves to be worshipped without partner. Allaah said,
Say: "Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, while He is the Lord of all things?
Ibn 'Abbaas said about the meaning of 'I seek a Lord' that it means 'God to be worshipped, Lord and Master.'

The saying 'while He is the Lord of all things' in the above aayah is explained by Ibn Jareer at-Tabaree as meaning 'He is the Lord and Master of everything besides Him. He is the disposer of affairs and the One that brings benefit.'

This is the strongest proof and the clearest evidence of the falsehood of shirk polytheism and taking partners. So whoever takes a Lord and Master other than Allaah, whether it is from the people of the graves or of the living, and he believes that he can bring benefit or repel harm; or he relies upon him for a need, or asks him to remove his worry, calamity or something like that, then he has committed shirk with Allaah the Mighty. Many nations have been put to trial with this belief so much so that some of them have been given this nickname of 'grave worshippers'. They believe in them, they turn to them, they are humble before them and with this they have negated their oneness of Allaah (tawheed) and have been polluted with what opposes and breaks it. Reflect upon the previous hadeeth of how the chosen Prophet ﷺ protected and saved tawheed and blocked the paths to shirk.

So when they said to him 'you are our master' He said, 'As-Sayyid The Lord and Master is Allaah'. Then he said to them 'and do not let the devil make you his agents' even though they only spoke the truth. For he ﷺ is the 'sayyid' head of the children of Aadam, the best of Allaah's servants and the leader of the pious. However, when Allaah perfected his ﷺ level of worship he disliked people praising him for it. He directed and advised the Ummah to leave this in order to protect the status of singling Allaah out alone for worship (tawheed) from what could enter, corrupt and weaken it with polytheism (shirk) and what leads to it which could direct the heart to a type of connection to the creation, humbling and lowering themselves to them which is not allowed or permissible to do except to Allaah, Al-Waahid The One, Al-Qahhaar The Invincible Subduer.

keyPoints: As-Sayyid is found in a hadeeth recorded by Aboo Daawood with a good chain, in which the Prophet ﷺ said: "The lord (sayyid) is Allah, the Blessed and Exalted."
Ibn 'Abbaas explained As-Samad (Ikhlaas 112:2) as: "Indeed He is the Master who is perfect in His Mastership."
Mastership in truth is only for Allaah: He alone actualizes mastership, ownership, creation and disposing of affairs, and He alone deserves to be worshipped without partner.
Whoever takes a Lord and Master other than Allaah, from the dead or the living, believing he can bring benefit or repel harm, or relying on him for a need, has committed shirk.
Although the Prophet ﷺ is the 'sayyid' of the children of Aadam, he disliked being praised this way in order to protect tawheed and block the paths to shirk.

evidence.text: "...we said: You are our lord (sayyid). To this he replied: The lord is Allah, the Blessed and Exalted..."
Say: "Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, while He is the Lord of all things?

recall.a: The Lord and Master; Mastership in truth is only for Allaah, who alone actualizes mastership, ownership, creation and disposing of affairs.

recall.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ reply when the deputation of Banoo 'Aamir said 'You are our lord (sayyid)'?
recall.a: "The lord is Allah, the Blessed and Exalted", and later: "Say what you have to say, or part of what you have to say, and do not let the devil make you his agents."
"Indeed He is the Master who is perfect in His Mastership."

recall.q: Why did the Prophet ﷺ dislike being called 'sayyid' even though it was true?
recall.a: To protect tawheed from what could corrupt and weaken it with shirk, and to block the paths leading the heart to humble itself to the creation.
